01-blog-sourdough.why: Y reads more naturally but adds the invented jar detail, while X sticks to the original facts.
X invents a detail (bubbling in its jar) and is slightly wordier; Y keeps the facts plainly.

02-blog-remote-work.why: Y is tighter, but it swaps the original's 'made all the difference' conclusion for a new 'on balance' verdict; X keeps it.
X reads more naturally but replaces the original's how-not-where conclusion, which Y keeps.

03-blog-product-launch.why: X adds an unsupported claim that working with clients abroad is as easy as working with local ones.
Y adds an unsupported claim that working with clients abroad is as easy as with local ones.

04-email-deadline.why: Both keep every fact, and Y's subject line and close read a bit more like a real email.
Both keep all facts; X's subject line and separate closing read a bit more like a real email.

05-email-followup.why: Both are faithful; Y's 'before then' closing is slightly awkward.
Y's 'I think a pilot would be a good place to start' stays closer to the original's endorsement than X's recast suggestion.

06-email-decline.why: Y avoids X's triplet list of Wen's qualities and reads more naturally; both keep all facts.
Both faithful; Y merges the thanks and decline more naturally.

07-tech-readme.why: X's prose reads like a real README but adds a mechanism explanation, while Y keeps the original claims more closely.
Y explains caching and TTL in clearer doc prose; both keep every fact.

08-tech-postmortem.why: Y's concrete lesson line beats X's leftover aphorism; both keep the 30% figure and avoid overclaims.
Both keep 30% and the facts; X turns the stock aphorism into a specific lesson.

09-tech-pr-description.why: X is a terse, natural PR description but drops the scalability claim, which Y keeps in hedged form.
Y is a cleaner, plainer PR description; both keep all facts.

10-essay-cities.why: X's ending is more concrete but invents an answer to who should decide, while Y keeps the original conclusion.
Y invents a new conclusion (cities decide for themselves and drop the mandate) instead of the original's call to embrace change.

11-essay-reading.why: X drops the essay's concluding point about stories, which Y keeps, though Y's ending is slightly stock.
Y drops the original's closing conclusion about the stories that stay with you.

12-essay-ai-art.why: Y is leaner, but it drops the personal reckoning and the closing claim about the technology's potential, which X keeps.
X avoids Y's leftover grand closing about the technology reaching its potential; both keep the facts.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: The replies are nearly identical, differing only in whether Aisha is named.
Both identical in substance; addressing Aisha fits a thread reply.

14-slack-meeting.why: Both keep the facts; Y's flow and closing sound more like a quick DM.
Both faithful; X reads as a tighter DM to a manager.

15-slack-review.why: Both are faithful; Y's paragraph split and colon explanation read more like a real review reply.
Both faithful; X's two short paragraphs read more like a natural review reply.

16-academic-abstract.why: X adds the correlational caveat and hedges the intervention claim, while Y still implies sleep would help students perform better.
Y states the correlational design and hedges accordingly, while X keeps the overclaim that improving sleep could help students perform better.

17-academic-discussion.why: X hedges the reliability and intervention claims more carefully, which is allowed weakening, while Y keeps the original's mild overclaims.
X keeps stronger claims (responses are reliable, a need for interventions) that Y appropriately softens.

18-academic-litreview.why: X changes 'numerous studies' to 'some studies', which alters what the Smith and Zhang citation claims.
Y changes the cited claim from 'numerous studies' to 'some studies', altering the strength of what Smith and Zhang is cited for.

19-report-quarterly.why: X says the pipeline 'may be the cause', which comes closer to naming a cause, while Y keeps 'one possible explanation'.
Y turns 'one possible explanation' into 'may be the cause', which edges toward naming a cause.

20-reflective-neutral.why: Y drops the closing reflection on teamwork and adapting, which X keeps in plain words.
Both keep the facts; Y ends with a modest version of the original's reflection instead of stopping abruptly.

21-slack-uncertain.why: Y strengthens 'might slip' to 'will probably slip' and drops 'about'.
X strengthens 'might slip' to 'will probably slip' and drops 'about'.

22-essay-example.why: Y drops the stock opener and hedges its closing line naturally; both keep the one-example and retirement caveats.
Y invents that the closure 'stayed with me' and calls it a sad reminder, adding feeling the writer did not express.

23-academic-correlation.why: Y keeps 'associated with' and 'self-reported' more precisely, while X turns the association into a plain statement that gym users had higher GPAs.
Y drops 'more often' from the gym-use finding and has a redundant 'instead...rather than'.
